accuracy.evidence: Matches the DfE National Curriculum (2013) Years 5-6 reading comprehension statutory requirements 'making comparisons within and across books' and 'identifying and discussing themes and conventions in and across a wide range of writing', and CCSS RL.5.9 'compare and contrast stories in the same genre on their approaches to similar themes and topics'. Terms are used correctly: first person ('I') vs third-person narrator ('he'), theme as the big idea, 'whereas' for contrast and 'similarly' for likeness. All numeric items (a-s, 2*(s+d), x+z, p-s) give positive whole answers at every range corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the 'two lists' answer (challenge 'list', m1, adult paragraph 2), the belief that a shared theme means a shared message (step 3 prediction 'brave is brave', m4, challenge 'same'), comparing surface features such as covers and page counts (m2, challenge 'cover'), using 'similarly' for a difference (step 5, challenge 'where' and 'how', m6) and putting shared features on one side of a Venn (challenge 'side' and 'out', p1).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbkcmp deals cards from two made-up novels one at a time into comparison zones: a Venn with own-side/middle bands, a 2x2 grid of character start/end for both heroes, and connective slots. flagrecbk (481) matches readers to books and builds a recommendation; flagnarr (212) is about unreliable narrators within one text. No existing lab compares two texts; the 30% shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Every card gets instant feedback that names the reason ('Only a first-person narrator can tell us feelings like "I hated". That is Nell.'); a wrong zone bounces the card and keeps it on top so the child retries. The steps build the method in order: same/different (Venn), how a theme is shown, how characters change, what the setting does, then joining both books in one sentence with the right connective.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions tested at once by the sort that follows: 'Will both authors show courage in the same way?' (tempting: yes, same theme = same writing), 'Do the two books say the same thing about courage?' (tempting: brave is brave), and 'Which word joins two things that are DIFFERENT?' (tempting: also/similarly). Each step's done message tells the child whether their prediction held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating Challenge questions with rotated answer order and 12 m= explanations, one for each wrong option (list, opin, cover, same, where, how, prob, time, side, out, talk, set), for example 'That is two facts side by side. A comparison joins them, with a word like "whereas".' Feedback sits in a polite live region with a streak counter.

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs for ages 10-11 that define each term as it appears (theme 'the big idea', narrator 'I' vs 'he or she') and pass the learner kid FK limit; card texts are one clause each. The adult text quotes the statutory wording, names the three common mistakes and lists the vocabulary to use.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job: what comparing is and the Venn, what to compare, same theme shown different ways, and how to write it up with connectives and evidence. The adult paragraphs give the curriculum, the mistakes, the terms and what the lab does. Numeric items use real Venn counting (x+z for one book's whole circle) rather than decoration.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark (r1403/bk-phone-*) show three readable columns with the own-side/middle bands, the 2x2 character grid, and one large card at the bottom with 'card 2 of 7'. Every zone has a full-width answer button below the canvas, so no fine dragging is needed; the walk gate passed every task on phone and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13. Each zone button has an aria-label naming the card and the zone ('Put "Told by Nell herself" in Only The Storm Lamp'); the canvas aria-label and live region read the reason after every placement and announce the next card; Challenge answers are real buttons in a labelled group.
